into which the cat fell.

The rat came out and crept along seeking something to eat, yet all the
while cautious, turning right and left. Upon seeing the cat in the snares, he rejoiced.

Then he turned around
and saw that a mongoose had tracked him and lay in wait, and looking over his head, he saw an owl, atop the tree, watching him.
And so, he feared-that if he turned back, the mongoose would jump on him; that if he moved left or right, the owl would snatch him;
and that if he stepped forward, the cat was right in front of him.

The rat said, “I need to
rely upon self-control, friendliness, and cunning to deal with this matter, so that I can escape from it,
for the hearts of the knowledgeable are a deep sea whose depth cannot be reached,

p.n: Situations Do Not Blind the Intelligent

body.p:
and trouble does not affect the men
of intelligence with the loss of sense; and neither should one reach a point where one doubts
oneself and becomes blind to one’s situation.”

p.n: The Rat Decides on a Pact with the Cat

body.p:
He then said: “I see no strategy more effective than to seek
reconciliation with the cat, for he has been beset by the kind of evil of which no one can rid him,
except me. He might, therefore, enter into an agreement with me to benefit himself, so that I too escape from
this evil I am verging upon.”

p.n: The Rat Comes Up to the Cat

body.p:
He approached the cat and said to him, ‘How
are you?’
He said, ‘As you would fancy-in dire straits. Why do you ask?’

p.n: The Rat Points Out Their Common Problem
